critical_code_review_comments: csl_espn_live.is_player_currently_active() semantics are tight: returns True on roster/leader hit (with espn_active=True), False on explicit inactive flag OR absent-from-all-indexes, and None ONLY if both caches are empty or the snapshot is older than DATA_STALE_AFTER_S (36h). The sportdb_player_scorer.py integration at lines 707-726 uses `verdict is False` to drop candidates — this is correct and matches the test expectation that None (unknown) DOES NOT drop the candidate. Guy Mbenza here returns False because his leaders-doc record carries active=False (he scored 9 goals in the season but is now transferred out), which is exactly the bug the user reported.

Mongo persistence in refresh() upserts into csl_espn_state with _id='active_roster' and 'season_leaders'. hydrate_from_db is idempotent and safe for repeated startup hits. No ObjectId leakage — both helpers use string `_id` keys.

Scheduler in arm_scheduler() is idempotent (`if _refresh_task and not _refresh_task.done(): return`) so server.py's hot-reload doesn't spawn duplicate refresh loops — confirmed by the single 'CSL ESPN live scheduler armed' log line per startup.

Name normalization (_norm + _resolve_alias + _name_match with Levenshtein≤1) correctly handles Crysan ≡ Cryzan as documented; verified live by the live_form snapshot returning team=Shandong Taishan for the query 'Crysan'.
The /api/picks/rollover endpoint correctly returns zero scorer-market entries — the existing soccer goal-scorer rollover block (separate from this iter) is unchanged and intact.

Auto-promotion of bossmanperkins@yahoo.com to admin role is wired and firing on every startup (`verified=False, aged_24h=True`) — admin HTTP routes are protected by `Depends(current_admin)` and reject the demo user with 403 as expected. This was visible in backend.out.log lines from a prior test attempt.
